name: Easy-Peasy.AI
summary: All-in-one AI platform for writing, images, audio transcription, text-to-speech and chatbots, with 200+ templates, a free plan and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
best_for: solo creators, marketers and small teams that want writing, images, transcription and voice in one subscription with a free tier to try first
skip_if: you need one model with predictable pricing, only need voice output, or want a tool we have tested on a paid plan ourselves
honest_knock: Allowances are counted in model-specific words and credits, so the usable amount depends on which model you pick. The pricing page quotes a 50% and a 40% yearly discount in different places. We have not paid for a plan, so output quality is untested by us.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month billed yearly ($96 a year)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on easy-peasy.ai/pricing, US dollars, unchanged since 2026-11-17, and in our own test that day) Free: $0, 1,000 words, 1 image credit, 1 transcription, 1,000 text-to-speech characters, 1 bot, 170+ templates, public images, no card. Starter: $8 a month billed yearly ($96 a year; $16 a month billed monthly), 25,000 Opus or 50,000 Sonnet, GPT-5 or Gemini Pro words, 200 image and video credits, 2 bots, 3 brand voices. Unlimited 50: $12 a month billed yearly ($144 a year; $24 monthly), unlimited standard model, 50,000 Opus or 100,000 Sonnet words, 300 credits, 3 bots. Unlimited: $16.50 a month billed yearly ($198 a year; $32 monthly), unlimited standard model, 100,000 Opus or 200,000 Sonnet words, 500 credits, 4 bots, API access, priority support. A 30-day money-back guarantee is stated. We have not paid for a plan. In our test on 18 November 2026 a new Free account showed '3 credits left' rather than 1, and one generated image used all 3, so Free covers about one image either way. The app's upgrade screen also showed a fifth plan that the pricing page does not list: Unlimited 200 at $28 a month billed yearly ($336 a year), with 200,000 Opus or 400,000 Sonnet words, 750 credits and 8 bots.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Easy-Peasy.AI in our existing free account: a Medium blog post about a made-up product came out at 1,772 words in about 30 seconds, left out the 12-hour battery fact from the prompt and added features that were not in it, and then the free word allowance was closed. One image took all 3 credits shown in the app, while the page says 1 image credit. The upgrade window showed a plan Unlimited 200 ($28 a month billed yearly, $336) that the dossier does not have. Only these two tools were tried, and no plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Easy-Peasy.AI our account, on the Free plan, with the interface already in English. No sign-up was done in this test. The test started at 08:53 on the dashboard, which showed Free and 3 credits left (also at the bottom of the left menu). The dossier name is Easy-Peasy.AI and the review page is on AIBM (b2b/easy-peasy-ai-review); the folder of the notes is easy-peasy and the review slug is easy-peasy-ai, so they differ. Core action, text: Home, All Tools, Instant Blog Post Generator (a guessed direct address gave a 404 page). Input: the topic Lumio X2, a made-up solar desk lamp with wireless charging and a 12-hour battery, 3 keywords, length Medium, language English, no tone of voice. Steps: 5 (open the tool, topic, keywords, length, Try Free). The first text appeared after about 10 seconds and the post was done after about 30 seconds (clock 08:54). The result was about 1,870 words by the tester count and 1,772 words in History, for a length that was set to Medium; at the bottom it said Generated with the free Standard model. and offered Regenerate with Advanced AI. The sidebar stayed at 3 credits left. Quality of the text, read critically: the stated fact of a 12-hour battery appears nowhere in the post (it says endless hours of light and hours of uninterrupted lighting). The post adds features that the prompt did not contain: adjustable brightness, color temperature modes, touch-sensitive controls, recyclable components, works even in low-light conditions and smart charge management. It contradicts itself with zero reliance on electricity next to a lamp that has a battery and a wireless charger. It leans on stock marketing phrases such as a Swiss Army knife of desk lamps and a beacon of innovation, it is long and repeats itself, and the comparison table against Traditional Desk Lamps is filled with assumptions such as Limited Settings and No Additional Features. Word limit: a click on Regenerate with Advanced AI gave at once Your plan has reached its word limit. To continue, please upgrade your plan., and a second Try Free gave the same notice. The free allowance of 1,000 words was therefore closed only after the first generation, which had produced 1,772 words; the check seems to happen before a run and not during it. Second function, images: AI Images (/ai-images) with the model GPT Image 2.6 Flare Medium. The button said Generate 3 credits. The prompt was a modern minimalist solar desk lamp on a wooden desk, an object and no people. The image was ready in under 10 seconds and was a usable product picture, with the solar panel but without the wireless charging pad. After it the counter said 0 credits and the page said You're out of image credits. Upgrade your plan to keep creating. Deviation from the dossier text on image credits: the dossier and the public pricing page say the Free plan has 1 image credit. In the app the Free account showed 3 credits left, and the single image with the standard model cost all 3. So one image was possible, but the unit is not what the page suggests: the credit in the app is a different count than the 1 on the page, and the dossier text is not taken over as a fact here. The 3 credits left at the start may be what remained of the free allowance of this existing account; that was not checked. Plans, read up to the payment step: the public page https://easy-peasy.ai/pricing (a logged-out view in the tab, with Log in and Sign up), yearly view, said literally: Free $0/month with 1,000 words, 1 image credit, 1 Audio transcriptions, 1,000 characters Text-to-Speech, 1 Bot, 170+ templates, Generated images are public, No parallel execution and No credit card required. Starter $8/month, billed yearly $192 $96, 25,000 Opus or 50,000 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini Pro words, 200 image/video credits, 20 Audio Transcriptions, 25,000 characters Text-to-Speech, 2 Bots and 3 Brand Voices. Unlimited 50 $12/month, $288 $144, 50,000 Opus or 100,000 Sonnet words, 300 image/video credits and 3 Bots. Unlimited $16.5/month, $384 $198, 100,000 Opus or 200,000 Sonnet words, 500 image/video credits, 4 Bots, API Access and Priority support. The page promises 100% no risk, 30-day money back guarantee. and has a switch Yearly billing -50%; the FAQ says there is a 40% discount if you choose the annual plan, which does not match the 50% on the switch; PayPal payment needs a request (please contact us). Deviation from the dossier, extra plan: the upgrade window in the app (after the word limit) showed four paid plans and no Free plan, the fourth being Unlimited 200 at $28/month, billed yearly $576 $336, with 200,000 Opus or 400,000 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini Pro words, 750 image/video credits, Unlimited Transcriptions, 120,000 characters Text-to-Speech and 8 Bots. The dossier does not have this plan, and the logged-out pricing page did not show it in the part that was read. All other prices and allowances matched the dossier word for word. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. Nothing was filled in and no Start button was clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not tested because there is no paid plan; the FAQ says You can easily cancel your subscription at any time by going to your account settings. Not tested: chat, video, audio and Text-to-Speech, transcription, bots, brand voices, the API, the paid models (Opus, Sonnet, GPT-5), Search the web, cancelling, refunds and the payment screen; chat, video, audio and transcription could not be tried because the credits were used up. Clean up: the blog post and the image were moved to the Trash through History; they still stand in the Trash tab, which was not emptied. The account and the Free plan stay. The tab was closed and no other tab was touched.
exit_test.awkward: The free word allowance of 1,000 words is checked before a run, so one Medium post of 1,772 words went through and the next run was blocked. The 12-hour battery from the prompt is missing in the text and several features were invented. One image took all 3 credits shown in the app, against 1 image credit on the page. The upgrade window has a plan that the pricing page read in the test did not show.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested Easy-Peasy.AI in our existing free account: a Medium blog post about a made-up product came out at 1,772 words in about 30 seconds, left out the 12-hour battery fact from the prompt and added features that were not in it, and then the free word allowance was closed. One image took all 3 credits shown in the app, while the page says 1 image credit. The upgrade window showed a plan Unlimited 200 ($28 a month billed yearly, $336) that the dossier does not have. Only these two tools were tried, and no plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Easy-Peasy.AI our account, on the Free plan, with the interface already in English. No sign-up was done in this test. The test started at 08:53 on the dashboard, which showed Free and 3 credits left (also at the bottom of the left menu). The dossier name is Easy-Peasy.AI and the review page is on AIBM (b2b/easy-peasy-ai-review); the folder of the notes is easy-peasy and the review slug is easy-peasy-ai, so they differ. Core action, text: Home, All Tools, Instant Blog Post Generator (a guessed direct address gave a 404 page). Input: the topic Lumio X2, a made-up solar desk lamp with wireless charging and a 12-hour battery, 3 keywords, length Medium, language English, no tone of voice. Steps: 5 (open the tool, topic, keywords, length, Try Free). The first text appeared after about 10 seconds and the post was done after about 30 seconds (clock 08:54). The result was about 1,870 words by the tester count and 1,772 words in History, for a length that was set to Medium; at the bottom it said Generated with the free Standard model. and offered Regenerate with Advanced AI. The sidebar stayed at 3 credits left. Quality of the text, read critically: the stated fact of a 12-hour battery appears nowhere in the post (it says endless hours of light and hours of uninterrupted lighting). The post adds features that the prompt did not contain: adjustable brightness, color temperature modes, touch-sensitive controls, recyclable components, works even in low-light conditions and smart charge management. It contradicts itself with zero reliance on electricity next to a lamp that has a battery and a wireless charger. It leans on stock marketing phrases such as a Swiss Army knife of desk lamps and a beacon of innovation, it is long and repeats itself, and the comparison table against Traditional Desk Lamps is filled with assumptions such as Limited Settings and No Additional Features. Word limit: a click on Regenerate with Advanced AI gave at once Your plan has reached its word limit. To continue, please upgrade your plan., and a second Try Free gave the same notice. The free allowance of 1,000 words was therefore closed only after the first generation, which had produced 1,772 words; the check seems to happen before a run and not during it. Second function, images: AI Images (/ai-images) with the model GPT Image 2.6 Flare Medium. The button said Generate 3 credits. The prompt was a modern minimalist solar desk lamp on a wooden desk, an object and no people. The image was ready in under 10 seconds and was a usable product picture, with the solar panel but without the wireless charging pad. After it the counter said 0 credits and the page said You're out of image credits. Upgrade your plan to keep creating. Deviation from the dossier text on image credits: the dossier and the public pricing page say the Free plan has 1 image credit. In the app the Free account showed 3 credits left, and the single image with the standard model cost all 3. So one image was possible, but the unit is not what the page suggests: the credit in the app is a different count than the 1 on the page, and the dossier text is not taken over as a fact here. The 3 credits left at the start may be what remained of the free allowance of this existing account; that was not checked. Plans, read up to the payment step: the public page https://easy-peasy.ai/pricing (a logged-out view in the tab, with Log in and Sign up), yearly view, said literally: Free $0/month with 1,000 words, 1 image credit, 1 Audio transcriptions, 1,000 characters Text-to-Speech, 1 Bot, 170+ templates, Generated images are public, No parallel execution and No credit card required. Starter $8/month, billed yearly $192 $96, 25,000 Opus or 50,000 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini Pro words, 200 image/video credits, 20 Audio Transcriptions, 25,000 characters Text-to-Speech, 2 Bots and 3 Brand Voices. Unlimited 50 $12/month, $288 $144, 50,000 Opus or 100,000 Sonnet words, 300 image/video credits and 3 Bots. Unlimited $16.5/month, $384 $198, 100,000 Opus or 200,000 Sonnet words, 500 image/video credits, 4 Bots, API Access and Priority support. The page promises 100% no risk, 30-day money back guarantee. and has a switch Yearly billing -50%; the FAQ says there is a 40% discount if you choose the annual plan, which does not match the 50% on the switch; PayPal payment needs a request (please contact us). Deviation from the dossier, extra plan: the upgrade window in the app (after the word limit) showed four paid plans and no Free plan, the fourth being Unlimited 200 at $28/month, billed yearly $576 $336, with 200,000 Opus or 400,000 Sonnet, GPT-5, Gemini Pro words, 750 image/video credits, Unlimited Transcriptions, 120,000 characters Text-to-Speech and 8 Bots. The dossier does not have this plan, and the logged-out pricing page did not show it in the part that was read. All other prices and allowances matched the dossier word for word. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached. Nothing was filled in and no Start button was clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not tested because there is no paid plan; the FAQ says You can easily cancel your subscription at any time by going to your account settings. Not tested: chat, video, audio and Text-to-Speech, transcription, bots, brand voices, the API, the paid models (Opus, Sonnet, GPT-5), Search the web, cancelling, refunds and the payment screen; chat, video, audio and transcription could not be tried because the credits were used up. Clean up: the blog post and the image were moved to the Trash through History; they still stand in the Trash tab, which was not emptied. The account and the Free plan stay. The tab was closed and no other tab was touched.
exit_test.awkward: The free word allowance of 1,000 words is checked before a run, so one Medium post of 1,772 words went through and the next run was blocked. The 12-hour battery from the prompt is missing in the text and several features were invented. One image took all 3 credits shown in the app, against 1 image credit on the page. The upgrade window has a plan that the pricing page read in the test did not show.
